# Stock Pulse

**A free, open-source alternative to Stock Events** — a portfolio & dividend tracker for **Android (APK + home-screen widgets)** and **Windows**, with no subscription, no account, and no API keys.

Built with Flutter. Market data comes from Yahoo Finance's public (unofficial) endpoints, which work without an API key.

<p align="center">
  <em>Portfolio value · daily change · dividend calendar · yield on cost · earnings dates · CSV import · home-screen widgets</em>
</p>

## Features

- 📈 **Multi-portfolio tracking** — stocks, ETFs, crypto (`BTC-USD`), foreign exchanges (`SHOP.TO`, `AIR.PA`, ...). Quantities and average cost merge automatically when you buy more of the same symbol.
- 🏛️ **Grouped by market** — holdings are split into exchange sections (NYSE, NASDAQ, TSX, TSX Venture, NYSE Arca, Crypto, …) using the venue each quote actually reports, so Canadian and US listings are never mixed up.
- 🖼️ **Real company logos** — each holding shows the issuer's own logo, served by Wikimedia Commons. A ticker is only matched when it maps to a single company, otherwise a letter badge is used.
- ⏱️ **Visible data freshness** — the exchange timestamp Yahoo reports is shown next to each quote, alongside the fetch time, so a delayed price is never presented as a live one.
- 💵 **Dividend tracking** — trailing-12-months income, annual income projection, portfolio yield & yield-on-cost, per-holding dividend history from 2 years of Yahoo data.
- 📅 **Dividend calendar** — a month view you can page through, with a tap on any day opening exactly what is scheduled that day. Below it, a month-by-month timeline of every upcoming dividend and earnings date, and a one-tap **export to your own calendar** (.ics).
- 🆕 **What's new** — dividends paid this month, paid so far this year, the biggest mover today, and the next event, in one card.
- 🕶️ **Hide balances** — one switch turns every amount into dots, for when you are not meant to be showing your screen.
- 🏭 **Industry breakdown** — allocation can be split by type, currency or industry, using the sector and industry Yahoo reports for each holding.
- 📊 **Interactive charts** — drag across the chart to scrub the exact value and date; the line draws itself in, the area is a soft gradient, and a **SPY benchmark overlay** stays legible but clearly secondary.
- 🧮 **Total return, honestly** — the return figure includes the dividends that were actually paid out, not just the price, and the chart has a **Total return** toggle that adds them back over time.
- 🧮 **Live KPI tiles** — today, total return, annual income and holdings, all counted up from real quote data, each one tappable through to the screen that explains it.
- 📈 **Per-holding sparklines** — a real one-month price trend next to every holding, from the same price history the charts use.
- 📰 **In-app news** — read a story inside the app with its image and the tickers it mentions (with live prices), then open the original with one tap.
- 📍 **52-week range bar** — on every holding, a marker shows exactly where today's price sits between the 52-week low and high.
- 🧾 **Bulk CSV import** — paste rows from your broker or open a `.csv` file. Column mapping is auto-detected and can be overridden. No more adding holdings one-by-one.
- 📤 **Export** — CSV of any portfolio, or a full JSON backup (restore on any device).
- 🔲 **Android home-screen widgets** — a value widget with a live trend line and a compact next-dividend widget, both in the app's own colours, updated hourly by a native WorkManager worker even when the app is closed. `tools/widget_preview.ps1` renders a picture of them so the design can be reviewed without a phone.
- 🌓 **Polished UI** — unified design system with theme-aware finance colors, shimmer skeletons, animated numbers, staggered list entrances, shared-axis page transitions, Hero avatar drill-downs, frosted-glass cards, and adaptive desktop/phone navigation.
- 💱 **FX display currency**, 🔒 **biometric lock**, ☁️ **private Gist sync**, 🔔 **local notifications** for dividends/earnings/price moves.

## Getting the app

### Android APK (recommended: let GitHub build it)

The included workflow builds a signed, sideloadable APK on every push:

1. Push the repo to GitHub (or fork it).
2. Open the **Actions** tab → latest **Build & Release** run → download the **StockPulse-android-apk** artifact.
3. Rename `app-release.apk` to `StockPulse.apk`, enable "Install unknown apps" for your browser/file manager, and install.

Tag a release (`git tag v1.2.0 && git push origin v1.2.0`) and the workflow also creates a GitHub Release with the APK, Windows zip, and web build attached.

### Play/publishing checklist

- **Data-safety:** portfolio symbols and quantities are local; optional Gist sync stores a full backup in the user's private Gist; Android ad requests send Google advertising/device data; optional diagnostics are user-controlled, local, and redacted.
- Verify a fresh-install APK: onboarding, quotes and chart retries, portfolio search/sort, dividends, import/export, widgets, biometric lock, and banner loading.
- Check AdMob **app readiness** and **Policy center**. Publishing consent messages does not by itself prove ad approval.

Portfolios are stored locally unless you enable Gist sync. Android includes a Google AdMob banner; the advertising SDK processes device/ad-request data separately from portfolio storage.

### Android advertising

Debug/profile builds use Google's test ads. Release builds use the AdMob placements below. Consent information is refreshed before requesting ads; when required, the app exposes **Ad privacy choices**. Configure the app's privacy policy and applicable consent messages in AdMob's **Privacy & messaging** console before distribution. Windows and web do not request mobile ads.

**Live ads are opt-in.** A release build serves Google's *test* ads unless it is built with `--dart-define=ADS_LIVE=true` (the CI release build turns them on only when the `ADS_LIVE` repository secret is set to `true`). AdMob asks for test ads while an app is under review, and it means an accidental click on a live ad cannot flag the account. See [`docs/PLAY_LAUNCH.md`](docs/PLAY_LAUNCH.md) for the full order of steps.

**Placements.** Each placement has its own ad unit so AdMob reports revenue per placement, which is what makes it possible to tell which one actually earns:

| Placement | Where it appears | Format | Ad unit |
|---|---|---|---|
| `holdings_native` | Below the holdings list | Native | `…/4150586198` |
| `news_native` | Every sixth story in the news feed | Native | `…/4150586198` |
| `news_article` | Inside an opened story | Native | `…/4150586198` |
| `dividends_native` | End of the dividends screen | Native | `…/4150586198` |
| `portfolio_banner` | Very end of the portfolio screen | Banner | `…/8657501940` |

All units belong to the app's AdMob account (`ca-app-pub-2085007206942111`, app `…~5871556500`). The native unit is shared by the four native placements: AdMob then reports them together, while the app's own placement report still separates them. **Separate native units per placement are better for ranking them** - create more in the console and point each placement at one from the developer panel.

Ad placement is a developer's decision, so there is no ad-unit setting in the app's normal settings — the unit editor is hidden behind five taps on the version number in **Settings → About**, and a blank ID simply hides that placement. The editor also shows the last load failure for each placement, so a blank slot can be explained without guessing.
**Why it does not feel like an ad app.** The rules are in `lib/services/ad_service.dart`:

- Ads sit *after* the content the user came for, never in front of it.
- A failed ad collapses to nothing, so the layout never shows a hole.
- Each placement is capped per day (native 3–6, banner 8) and all placements together are capped per session, so the app cannot turn into a slot machine.
- A placement never repeats within three minutes.
- Native ads are labelled "Sponsored".

**There is no ad switch, and that is deliberate.** Stock Pulse is free because it carries ads - there is no paid tier to upgrade to, so an "ad-free" toggle would be a lie. What the user *can* do is consent: **Settings → Advertising → Ad privacy choices** opens Google's privacy form, which decides what the ad SDK may share about the device. That is a different thing from turning ads off, and it is required for users in the EEA, the UK, Switzerland and the US states. Ads are still shown; they just carry less information.

**Measuring it.** The developer panel (five taps on the version number in **Settings → About**) shows a **placement report**: impressions, clicks and estimated revenue per placement, taken from the ad SDK's own paid-event reporting. It is stored on the device only - nothing is sent to a server - so the ad units can be judged on evidence instead of guesswork.

**Going live checklist.** Everything the app needs is in the build; the rest is in the AdMob console:

1. The **app id** (`ca-app-pub-2085007206942111~5871556500`) is in `AndroidManifest.xml`, and the ad units are compiled into `lib/services/ad_service.dart`.
2. The app needs a **privacy policy URL** and completed **app privacy details** in AdMob, or the account will not serve.
3. The app's **readiness status** in AdMob must allow serving. An app that is still "Under review" only serves test ads.
4. For US and EEA users, publish a **consent message** in AdMob's Privacy & messaging console. Canadian users do not normally see one.
5. Test the **placement report** in Settings → Advertising after a few days of real use; that is the number to judge placements by.
6. Never click your own live ads - that is a policy violation and can suspend the account.

### Publishing on the Play Store

[`docs/PLAY_LAUNCH.md`](docs/PLAY_LAUNCH.md) walks through it: creating an upload keystore, giving CI the signing secrets, building a signed `.aab` alongside the APK, creating the Play listing, linking the app in AdMob (which is what lifts "Limited ad serving"), and hosting `app-ads.txt` on the domain listed in the store listing. The repository already contains `app-ads.txt`, and the web build publishes it at its root.

The launcher/splash artwork is generated from `tools/icon.ps1` into `assets/icon/`. Run that script, `dart run flutter_launcher_icons`, and `dart run flutter_native_splash:create` after changing the artwork.

The artwork and the in-app icon share one geometry definition (`PulseLogoGeometry` in `lib/widgets/pulse_logo.dart`), and `test/app_icon_consistency_test.dart` checks the committed PNG still matches it — so the icon on the home screen and the icon inside the app cannot drift apart.

### 1.3 dashboard update

- Larger balance summary, a focused performance panel, and a cleaner mobile navigation bar.
- Toggle SPY comparison, drag the chart for dated values, search holdings, and sort by symbol or daily percentage change.
- Tap upcoming events to open the holding; tab switches preserve screen state and the banner instance.
- Chart requests are reused across dashboard interactions, with a retry action for failures.
- Ad loading remains gated by Google's consent status, with stale-callback protection and recoverable privacy-form errors.

For device verification, use debug/profile builds and Google's test ads. Check banner loading, tab switching, privacy choices where required, and offline startup. European/US messages do not normally appear for Canadian users. A published consent message is not itself confirmation of AdMob app approval: check the app readiness status and Policy center in AdMob. Build checks do not replace on-device consent testing.

### Windows

The same workflow produces a **StockPulse-windows** artifact (a zip of the Release build). Unzip and run `stock_pulse.exe`.

## Importing your portfolio

The **Import** tab accepts:

| Format | Example |
|---|---|
| Comma / semicolon / tab CSV (file or pasted) | `AAPL,10,101.50` |
| With headers | `Ticker,Quantity,Avg Cost` / `Symbol;Shares;Price` |
| Broker-ish exports with extra columns | any columns — mapping is detected, and you can override it in the UI |
| Quoted fields | `"MSFT","Company, Inc.",4,"1,234.50"` |
| Decimal commas / currency labels | `1,5` → 1.5 · `USD 10.50` → 10.50 |
| Duplicates | merged: quantities add, average cost re-weights |

Minimum: a **symbol** and a **quantity** column (avg cost optional — yield-on-cost simply won't show for those rows).

Sample:

```csv
Symbol,Quantity,AvgCost
AAPL,10,101.50
SCHD,55,
MSFT,4,243.20
SHOP.TO,15,
BTC-USD,0.25,58000
```

You can also **export** any portfolio back to CSV, or take a full JSON backup (Settings → Data) to move devices.

## Widgets (Android)

After installing, add them from the home screen: **long-press wallpaper → Widgets → Stock Pulse**

- **Stock Pulse** — total portfolio value, daily change (color-coded), next dividend.
- **Next Dividend** — compact "symbol · amount · dates" widget.

The app updates both widgets whenever quotes refresh (app open, pull-to-refresh, manual). Data lives in `HomeWidgetPlugin` SharedPreferences; no network access happens in the widget itself.

## Building locally

Install [Flutter](https://docs.flutter.dev/get-started/install) (3.27+), then:

```bash
# generate platform folders and apply the Android widget overlay
./scripts/setup_platforms.sh          # or on Windows:
powershell ./scripts/setup_platforms.ps1 [-Windows]

flutter run -d windows                # desktop app
flutter run                           # on a connected Android device
flutter build apk --release           # APK -> build/app/outputs/flutter-apk/
```

> Platform folders (`android/`, `windows/`) are gitignored — `flutter create` regenerates them in CI, and `platform_overlay/android/` is copied over the generated `android/` folder to install the widget providers, app id (`app.stockpulse`), and manifest.

Run tests: `flutter test`

## How it works

```
lib/
├── models/            Holding, Portfolio, Quote, DividendInfo/UpcomingDividend
├── services/
│   ├── yahoo_service.dart   unofficial Yahoo client (cookie+crumb handshake,
│   │                        batched v7 quotes, v8 chart fallback, search, news,
│   │                        quoteSummary calendarEvents)
│   ├── logo_service.dart    company logo lookup (curated ticker map +
│   │                        ticker-matched Wikidata query, logos from Wikimedia)
│   ├── store.dart           JSON file persistence (portfolios + cache)
│   ├── csv_import.dart      pure-Dart CSV/TSV parser & column detection
│   ├── export_service.dart  save dialog (desktop) / share sheet (Android)
│   └── widget_service.dart  home_widget bridge (no-ops off Android)
├── providers/portfolio_provider.dart  state, refresh pipeline, computations
└── screens/           portfolio, detail, dividends/calendar, news, import, settings
platform_overlay/android/            native widget providers (Kotlin) + layouts
.github/workflows/build.yml          analyze+test, APK, Windows zip, tagged releases
```

**Market grouping**: Yahoo reports a venue code (`NMS`, `NYQ`, `TOR`, …) and a venue name (`NasdaqGS`, `NYSE`, `Toronto`, …) per quote. The app normalises those into a market label, preferring the code because several venues share a name. Only well-known symbol suffixes (`.TO`, `.V`, `.L`, …) are used as a last resort, and a holding whose market genuinely cannot be determined is shown under **Other** rather than being guessed.

**Company logos**: well-known tickers are hardcoded to a Wikimedia Commons file. Anything else is resolved by asking Wikidata which company claims that exact ticker symbol, then matching the candidate against the company name the quote carries — so `C` resolves to Citigroup rather than a different company that shares the ticker. If no candidate matches confidently, the holding keeps its letter badge. Wikimedia serves the images with permissive CORS headers, so the same URLs work on Android, Windows and the web.

**App icon**: `tools/icon.ps1` draws the launcher and splash artwork from the same geometry as `lib/widgets/pulse_logo.dart`, so the icon on the home screen is the same picture as the icon inside the app.

**Dividend dates**: when Yahoo's `calendarEvents` module returns an upcoming ex-dividend/pay date it is used verbatim; otherwise the next dates are extrapolated from the median gap between the last payments (quarterly ≈ 91 days, monthly ≈ 30, ...). Amounts per share come from the payment history (or `trailingAnnualDividendRate`).

**Caching**: quotes are written to disk on every refresh, so the app renders instantly next launch; dividend calendar data is cached 24h; charts 10 min; news 15 min. Requests are staggered to stay polite to Yahoo's free endpoints.

## Web version (bonus)

Every push also builds a **Flutter web** release (`StockPulse-web` artifact). Browsers can't call Yahoo directly (no CORS), and the cookie/crumb handshake needs reading `Set-Cookie`, which JavaScript is never allowed to read — so the repo ships a tiny **Cloudflare Worker** proxy (`cloudflare/`) that:

- forwards requests to an allow-list of Yahoo hosts,
- re-exposes Yahoo's `Set-Cookie` as a readable `x-set-cookie` header,
- forwards your `Cookie` header for the crumb handshake,
- answers CORS preflights.

To use it:
1. Deploy from the repo:  `cd cloudflare && npx wrangler deploy` (needs a free Cloudflare account; you already deploy via Wrangler for other sites).
2. Open the web app (serve the artifact or a Pages deployment) → Settings → **Web build** → paste your proxy URL (`https://yahoo-proxy.<yoursubdomain>.workers.dev`).

Data on web lives in your browser's localStorage; export/backup still works (saved to clipboard on web).

## Disclaimer

Prices and dividend/earnings dates are from Yahoo Finance's unofficial API and may be delayed, missing or wrong. Estimates are marked with `*` in-app. This tool tracks *your* numbers; it is **not** investment advice. Yahoo data use is subject to their terms; consider contributing to a paid alternative you like if you need guarantees.

Company logos are served by Wikimedia Commons and remain under their respective owners' terms; a logo is only shown when the ticker maps unambiguously to one company.
